subtype: Approach: gathering specific examples before speaking [Thinking]
passage: I'm Hafsa, and I sit next to Nikhil's desk. Before he spoke to Tanish last Thursday, I watched Nikhil open a notes file and type a list: three tasks handed in late this month, two changes pushed without tests. He wrote down the dates. Then he deleted the word "careless" from the top line and typed "what happened". Through the glass I heard: "Three tasks came in after their dates, and two changes went out untested. Help me understand what was going on." Tanish looked at the table for a moment and then began to talk. I can't say what Nikhil was thinking. But it looked as if he wanted the conversation to stay on the work.

qa.q: How many tasks were handed in late this month?
qa.a: Three tasks were handed in late this month.

qa.q: What might Nikhil have been feeling when deleting the word "careless"?
qa.a: Nikhil seems to have been concerned about being fair and wanted to avoid a label that would make Tanish defensive, though Hafsa can only guess.

qa.q: What else could Nikhil do in the talk, and why?
qa.a: Nikhil could ask Tanish what would make it easier to finish tasks and test changes, because the answer shows whether the problem is effort, skill or support.

qa.q: How might Tanish have felt hearing dates and facts instead of a label?
qa.a: Tanish was probably nervous but relieved to be asked about what happened, which makes it easier to answer honestly.

grounding: Illustrates a lead listing what actually happened, three late tasks and two untested changes, and avoiding labels so the talk stays on observable work.
